newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes broadly steady, Brent falters.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes broadly steady, Brent falters.

text.p: North Sea crudes were broadly steady Thursday although a recent rally in Dated Brent, partly fuelled by U.S. demand, appeared to falter, traders said.

The marker crude traded at parity to Dated Brent quotes for the remainder of this week for a Dec 17-19 cargo, equivalent to about Jan Brent +35/+40 cents. Brent traded twice on Wednesday at Jan +35 and +49 cents.

The clocking of one of Thursday's two cargoes -- to Norway's Statoil -- also took some of the wind out of Brent's sails, traders said. The other cargo, due to load Dec 20-22, was kept by Wall Street trader J.P. Morgan.
One of Wednesday's buyers -- another Wall Street trader seen planning a transatlantic trip -- had collected enough cargoes to fill a VLCC, traders said.
Brent paper was firm, mirroring gains on the Jan IPE futures contract, which added 29 cents to $24.07 a barrel by 1837 GMT. Jan/Feb was talked at +72/+77 cents and Feb/Mar at +69/+74 cents.
Brent CFDs for next week gained eight cents to trade at Jan Brent +38 cents, while the following week lagged at +5/+9 cents.
Other North Sea grades were quiet with unsold December supply limited to a couple of Oseberg, Ekofisk and Gullfaks A.
